messages:
matt: Quick heads-up — we've flagged a rising rate of ECC/Xid errors on a subset of Dedicated GPU hosts in eu-central-1 (nodes gded-42*, gded-43*). Pattern looks like intermittent GPU ECC corrective events that correlate with driver 535.x on these machines. Ops recommends rotating the affected GPUs and proactively replacing the cards during a maintenance window.

jess: How customer-impacting is this? will there be failovers or dropped capacity?

matt: Short answer: we expect automatic workload failover to other racks for most tenants, but for some pinned Dedicated pools there will be a brief draining window per host (~10-15m) while we swap cards. No data will be lost; KV caches will be cold after restart.

ajay: Capacity note — eu-central-1 reserved pools are at ~78% utilization today. If we take 2 hosts at a time for replacement we'll keep within SLA by routing to burst capacity and compatible model variants. I'll open a temporary scale target.

olivia: Drafting customer-facing copy below — please review for tone and operational details. target is Dedicated & Private customers who have pinned hosts in eu-central-1.

matt: Paste the draft here and we'll iterate.

olivia: ```
Hi — This is Redwood Inference Ops with a proactive maintenance notice for Dedicated/Private customers in eu-central-1.

What happened: We observed recurring ECC and Xid errors on a small set of GPU devices serving Dedicated capacity. These errors increase the risk of degraded inference performance and, in rare cases, can lead to host reboots.

What we’re doing: To prevent user-facing interruptions, we will rotate and replace the affected GPU cards during a short maintenance window. Each host will be drained, the GPU swapped, and the host brought back into service. Workloads on other hosts will handle traffic during the operation.

Timing: Planned window: 2027-09-21 02:00–06:00 UTC. We will perform replacements in small batches (1–2 hosts at a time) to minimize impact.

Impact: Most customers will see no interruption. Customers using pinned Dedicated capacity or strict placement constraints may observe a temporary increase in latency or brief cold-cache effects (~10–20 minutes per affected host). No customer data will be modified or deleted.

What you can do: If you have strict SLAs or pinned placement, reply to this message or open a support ticket and we'll provide a targeted plan and can postpone or coordinate a custom window.

Contact: support@redwood.ai (support portal link) — we’ll post live updates to this thread during the maintenance.

Thanks,
Redwood Ops
```

jess: LGTM. Add a line about fallback routing to compatible model variants (we should call out that small-model fallbacks may be used)

olivia: Updated draft with fallback note and a short FAQ.

matt: Ops runbook checklist (internal):
```
- identify affected hosts: gded-4232..gded-4239, gded-4310..gded-4313
- notify customers via email+portal post
- set drain policy: immediate soft-drain, 10m grace
- scale up burst pools in eu-central-1 by +2 hosts pre-window
- perform card swap, run health checks, validate driver stability
- post-maintenance: monitor Xid/ECC counters for 24h
```

leah: I'll own customer notifications. I'll queue the email and post in the portal once we lock the window. I'll also tag any customers with pinned placement. :white_check_mark:

support-bot: Created ticket RED-32419 for eu-central-1 Dedicated GPU replacements. SLA escalation route set to Tier 2 on-call.

ops-bot: Canary tests scheduled at 02:15 UTC, 02:45 UTC, 03:30 UTC for each replacement batch.

ajay: One more ask — include a short note in the customer message about potential temporary billing variance if we route to burst capacity (very small delta, we will absorb excess for impacted customers during maintenance).

olivia: Done — added a billing note and a contact for billing questions.

matt: Final steps: leah will send the customer notice. ajay will increase burst capacity. ops team will execute the rotation with canaries and post live updates here. If no objections by EOD UTC we'll schedule the window. :thumbsup:

leah: No objections from me. Scheduling and sending at 18:00 UTC today.

jess: Thanks team. I'll standby for any support escalations.

matt: Thanks — keeping this thread as the live update channel during the window.
